slot_note: Forecasting lane. Architecture 4 leaves banking for urban-regional-science forecasting: a New Zealand forestry company's log truck loads to its export port once the 50MAX route opens, each load's gain capped by its bunks' volume as well as by the new mass limit.
niche: a plantation forestry company's forecast of the FY2028 log truck loads from its forests to the export port once the 50MAX permits open the route, each load's payload limited by the new gross mass less its unit's tare and by the volume its bunks hold for the grade's log length, read by linking the weighbridge tickets to the port's log scaling records
answer: 29,000 export log loads to Port Kowhai in FY2028 under the 50MAX route limits, to the nearest 500 (A grade 4,900; Pruned 2,500; K grade 7,500; KI grade 8,000; KIS grade 6,100, each to the nearest 100)
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the 50MAX approval, the fleet register and the harvest plan correctly, lets every 50MAX permit unit's load rise to 50 tonnes gross less its tare and divides the plan's tonnes by the new average payloads files 27,000 loads (26,787 unrounded), about 2,200 short, because the short-length grades fill their bunks before they reach 50 tonnes.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each log truck load's payload under the FY2028 route limits, which log transport planning gets from the unit's gross mass limit less its tare and the volume its bunks hold for the logs' length at the load's density; with another field's nouns the gross mass limit, the tare, the bunk volume by log length and the JAS volume per load have nothing to attach to.
layer1: weighbridge tickets carrying net mass only, the unit's tare kept in the fleet register, two trucks re-registered on personalised plates mid-year
port log scaling records stamped by the scaling station's clock, keyed to the truck registration rather than the weighbridge ticket, a few minutes after the weighbridge time
JAS volumes per load beside green tonnes, grades coded on the tickets and named in the plan, log lengths only in the export grade specification
a fleet register numbered by Matiri's induction across carriers, tares varying with configuration, bunk count, age and fit-out
cartage invoices with subcontracted trucks billed under the head contractor's carrier code and credit notes reversing lines billed twice
mill dockets dated when posted, days after delivery, the delivery date only in the mills' weighbridge logs among other suppliers' trucks
stakeholder_role: haulage manager at a forestry company, sizing the FY2028 cartage contract

spine.entity: one log truck load weighed at the port

world.org_type: plantation forestry company exporting logs through a regional port

driver: Raising the limit that binds a unit's load lifts it only until the next limit binds, and for a large share of units the next limit is a capacity in another dimension that the old limit had left with little headroom; letting every unit rise to the new limit, or only the units that sat at the old one, files the units needed low.
driver_concrete: Matiri Forest Products sizes its FY2028 cartage by dividing the harvest plan's tonnes by each grade's payload under the 50MAX limits, but a load gains mass only until its bunks are full: the port's scaling volumes, linked to the weighbridge tickets by truck and time, give each load's density, the fleet register gives each unit's bunk volume for the grade's log length, and the short grades reach full bunks a few tonnes above today's loads, so the mass-only uplift files the FY2028 loads well short.
stump: A strong solver lets each 50MAX permit unit's load rise to 50 tonnes gross less its tare and files 27,000 loads; the step that lands it there is ignoring the bunks: the scaling volumes and the register's full-bunk volumes show the short-length grades fill their bunks a few tonnes above today's payloads, so they gain a fraction of the six tonnes the new limit allows and FY2028 needs 29,000 loads.

differentiation.task141: task141 prices units whose term has or lacks room under a ceiling, and its earlier architectures an offsetting term filed under another key or outcomes seen only for units let through; here no term, outcome or offset is priced: each load's payload rises with a relaxed mass limit only until its bunks are full, read per load from linked weighbridge and scaling records.
differentiation.task142: task142 builds an upper percentile of a period total from arrivals and durations counted inside a window; here no percentile, arrival or duration is built: a load's payload is capped by its unit's tare under the new gross limit and by its bunks' volume at the load's own density.
differentiation.task148: task148 drains a queue by units that give up waiting, and its first architecture sums hazards behind a shared backer; here nothing waits, fails or is shared: each load's gain under a higher mass limit stops at the bunk volume for its logs' length.
differentiation.task173: task173 adds a work-induced failure chance per scheduled visit, and its second architecture prices replacement volume from a second source sharing a meter; here no failure, visit or second source enters: a relaxed mass limit lifts each load only until the next physical limit, its bunks' volume, binds.
differentiation.task133: the slot's architecture 3 read a sector scenario through the industries paying each borrower and was spent on an unfiled transmission convention; architecture 4 forecasts truck loads whose payload gain is capped physically by bunk volume, with no convention between the scenario and the unit.
differentiation.task134: task134 forecasts homes from lots whose raised allowance pays only once the best permitted option out-earns what stands there; here no option is chosen and nothing is rebuilt: a relaxed vehicle mass limit lifts each log load only until its bunks are full, read per load from linked weighbridge and scaling records against the fleet register's volumes.

lineage.fate: hardening loop 1: survival to date landed on the portal (one model stumped, the other filed AUD 13,773,000 and scored 100 per cent, banking every inheriting ask: stage by product, drawdown year, stage 3 count)
lineage.driver: A cumulative outcome curve is filed from each unit's entry, and every unit in scope has already survived part of it, so its forward probability is the curve's remaining increments divided by its own survival to date; reading the curve from entry for every unit overstates the total, and shifting it to the unit's age without the division understates it.
lineage.stump: A competent solver applies the cumulative PD curve to each loan's remaining months counted from the reporting date as if it were a term structure and books an allowance about 43 per cent high; the step that lands it there is reading a curve indexed by months on book as if every performing loan were new.

lineage.fate: round 2 (2026-10-14): never judged on the portal; the 10/10 audit found it compliant but weak: a rung added above the step the v1 portal winner solved, with the development sample's outcome column beside a 'share of every loan drawn' header signposting it
lineage.driver: A cumulative outcome curve is filed as shares of every unit that ever entered, so units that left by a competing exit stay in its base; a unit still in scope at its age has come through both the outcome and the competing exit, so its forward probability is the curve's increment divided by the share of entrants still present and outcome-free at that age, which only the unit-level development record gives; dividing by one less the curve to date leaves the exited units in the base and understates the total, and a hazard rolled forward with no competing exit overstates it.
lineage.stump: A competent solver reads the PD curve as cumulative default by months on book, divides each loan's forward increments by its survival to date, 1 - C(a), and books about AUD 11.74 million against AUD 13,160,000, 10.8 per cent low; the step that lands it there is taking the curve's shares as shares of loans still open when they are shares of every loan drawn, so the loans repaid in full by month a stay in the at-risk base.

lineage.architecture: v2 (round 2, left truncation in the loan record)
lineage.fate: landed on the portal (the survival-to-date conditioning was the field's reflex); re-rooted 2026-11-01 at the Batch 3 queue reset (one architecture per world: the Bellbird personal-loan ECL world is closed)
lineage.driver: A unit-level record that took over an earlier record's units holds them only if they were still present at the takeover, so the months they spent before it are months the record never watched, not months they were seen to come through; outcome rates by age must count each taken-over unit only from its age at the takeover, and counting it from its own start fills every early age's denominator with exposure that could not end in the outcome, so the rates and the forward total for a young population come out low.
lineage.stump: A strong solver builds each product's monthly default and repayment rates by month on book from the loan record, counting every loan from its drawdown, rolls each performing loan forward from its own month on book, and books AUD 11.6 million against AUD 13.2 million (12.3 per cent low); the step that lands it there is counting the 16,479 loans the record took over at the October 2019 go-live as at risk from their drawdown, when the record holds them only because they were still open that day.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-01 at stage 4: the judge returned NOT_DETERMINISTIC with SOLUTION_WRONG, SEND_BACK, its Gate H line reading 'decisive_step analytical only if the method is filed' (CR-ST-02 2.1 and 3.2 read word for word give each borrower its own NZBN division's change, NZD 10.0 million, the default path; the payer route was an unfiled transmission convention, Gates B, C, E); the leak reader's question 6 read the call as following a stated rule plus reading fields and codes correctly; the asks rested on unfiled choices
lineage.driver: A unit's loss under a shock that hits groups of others unevenly is set by the share of its income each group pays it, read from who pays it, and it responds to its own income loss along a steep curve, so mapping each unit to the shock its own label names leaves units paid by the hardest-hit groups at a mild rate, overstates units of a hard-hit label paid by sheltered groups, and files the total low.
lineage.stump: A strong solver stresses each business borrower at the scenario's sales path for its own ANZSIC division, applies the revenue-shock PD table, the stressed LGDs and EAD, and files NZD 10.0 million; the step that lands it there is reading each borrower's sales fall off its own industry when its receipts show who pays it, and the builders, hotels and tour operators that pay much of the book cut their spending by a quarter.
